subject: Observability egress: authz, SIEM contracts, and fallback routing
messages:

Subject: Observability export requirements for private cluster

Markus / team,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. We sketched out our constraints and the handful of questions that matter for security sign-off. High level: Acme will run Redwood inside our VPC with no outbound NAT to the public internet, and we need a deterministic plan for observability exports that meets our SOC2 evidence retention and SIEM ingestion timelines.

Questions we need answered before we move to procurement:
- What authentication modes are supported for on-prem forwarders (mTLS, token, signed JWT)?
- Can we run a push-based forwarder from the customer side to a private Splunk HEC in our VNets, or does Redwood require a pull/polling agent inbound?
- What evidence/bundles are produced for audits (log bundles with integrity proofs)?
- Fallback: if the private forwarder fails, what are the automated fallback behaviors (local queueing, S3 egress to customer-controlled bucket, backoff windows)?

I've attached our SIEM requirement doc (acme_siem_requirements.pdf). Could you reply with the minimal architecture sketch + a short checklist we can hand to our infosec team?

Best,
Tom
Tom Reilly
Head of Infra Ops, Acme Corporation

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Observability export requirements for private cluster

Tom — thanks, clear ask. Short answers up front, then a recommended authn/authz flow and fallback choices.

1) Supported auth modes: mTLS (recommended), bearer token (scoped, short-lived), and signed JWT for cross-account automation. For private deployments we typically recommend mTLS + client cert rotation via customer KMS/HSM or Redwood-managed certs into a private CA.

2) Push vs pull: Redwood supports both patterns depending on the customer topology. For fully air-gapped VPCs we support a customer-side forwarder that pushes to an internal Splunk HEC endpoint (push). Alternatively, customers can install our forwarder as a sidecar that writes to a customer-owned S3 endpoint (signed PUTs) which their SIEM polls. Pull from Redwood-controlled endpoints is not allowed for private/no-egress setups.

3) Audit evidence: we can produce time-ordered log bundles with SHA256 manifests and OPTIONAL signed metadata (signed by Redwood service-key). For customers needing custody proofs, we can optionally sign manifests with a customer-provided key (HSM-backed) so the audit trail is verifiable.

4) Fallback behavior: default is local disk-backed buffering with configurable retention window (48–168h), exponential backoff for retries, and a configurable fallback to customer-controlled S3 (signed, private bucket). Important: automatic outbound egress to Redwood-managed storage is disabled in private deployments unless explicitly authorized.

Attached is a suggested config snippet and a concise checklist. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min whiteboard to map the flow into your network diagram.

Action items for Acme to unblock:
- Confirm preferred auth mode (mTLS vs tokens).
- Confirm Splunk HEC endpoint details + cert distro path (if mTLS).
- Decide fallback storage (local only vs S3).

Thanks,
Markus Klein
VP, Product — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Tom — quick compliance notes from our side:

- Evidence retention: we can align our retention windows to your stated policy, but data residency requires configs to point at customer-managed storage for long tail retention.
- Signed manifests: to support your SOC2 auditor we recommend enabling "customer-sign" mode during rollout (we'll provide the HSM integration doc).
- Access control: RBAC for who can request evidence exports is enforced at the console; for private deployments you can map AD groups to console roles.

One implementation detail to flag: if you ask for mTLS with mutual client certs, we'll need a mechanism for cert rotation and revocation lists. For full compliance we recommend putting an automation job in your CA to rotate certs every 30 days and push new certs to the forwarder config via your config management system.

I'll add a short checklist to the Drive link Markus provided and drop a CAB-friendly summary.

—Kimberly
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Observability export requirements for private cluster

Tom — following up with an example fallback orchestration and a lightweight runbook. I've pasted the key snippet below and attached an audit checklist.

--- pasted runbook excerpt ---
1) Forwarder process runs in customer VPC with local disk buffer (config: buffer.max_bytes=10GB; buffer.sync_interval=30s).
2) On HEC auth failure: escalate to token refresh (if token mode) or rotate certs (mTLS). Retries: 5 attempts with exponential backoff (base 2s).
3) After retries exhausted: push batches to customer S3 endpoint (signed PUT) using short-lived STS creds; mark bundle with manifest.json (sha256 checksums) and evidence_stamp.sig (customer-signed optional).
4) Audit bundle retention: default 90 days in local buffer index; export copies to S3 retained per your policy.
--- end excerpt ---

Attachments: evidence-handshake-checklist.xlsx (contains the handover steps for your SOC). We can also produce a minimal network ACL list you can hand to your networking team (source IP ranges, required ports: 9411 for tracing, 8088 for Splunk HEC, 443 for S3).

I can open a short support ticket to generate a sample manifest bundle for your SIEM team to validate ingest. Do you want that?

Jordan Blake
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
